exposure: dynamic ultrasound monitoring (fetal position, angle of progression (AOP), head-perineum distance (HPD))
cohort: The study included 60 pregnant women experiencing slow second stage of labor (SSL).
finding: Dynamic intrapartum ultrasound monitoring, utilizing AOP and HPD, significantly reduced the cesarean section rate, perineal lacerations, and postpartum blood loss while improving assisted vaginal delivery success compared to traditional digital examination.
mod_finding: The ultrasound monitoring group demonstrated a significantly lower cesarean section rate (23.3% vs. 40.0%) and higher assisted vaginal delivery success (86.7% vs. 66.7%) compared to the digital examination group.
